messages:
Jess (runtime): FYI rolling canary v1.12 -> multiple prod shards. Seeing p95/p99 spike starting ~10:12 UTC on canary nodes. Topline: p95 ~250ms -> 420ms, p99 ~620ms -> 1.4s. Not all regions impacted. :thinking_face:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: p99_latency(service=\"inference-runtime\",deployment=\"canary\") crossed 1s at 2026-03-12T10:12:34Z. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/runtime-latency?orgId=1&from=now-1h :warning:
Jess (runtime): attaching quick diff of canary changes: kernel selector bump + batching heuristics tweak + kv-cache hotkey.
```
- kernel_selection: default -> prefer_fast_math
- batching: max_batch_ms: 8 -> 16
- kv_cache: aggressive_prefix_prune: true
```
Pranav (infra): thanks. First pass: is the spike correlating to request size or seq length? can you paste p99 by seq_len bucket? :eyes:
Jess (runtime): added quick panel. p99 for seq<=64 barely changed. seq 512-1024 jumps the most. looks like high-seqlen requests routed to canary nodes more (routing policy change in rollout).
Eva (ml-infra): the kernel selector change could regress long-sequence perf on certain kernels (fp16 vs int8 paths). Does canary use different quantized kernel?
Jess (runtime): canary nodes are using new compiled kernels (jit-1.7) and changed fallback ordering.
Sahil (runtime): also noticed batching window increased (8->16ms). that increases tail latency if some requests are blocked waiting. For p99 that can matter.
Kate (sre): recap: suspects = (1) new kernel selection, (2) batching window change, (3) routing producing hot long-seq traffic on canary. Recommend triage steps: a) isolate canary nodes, b) reproduce with synthetic long-seq load, c) bisect config/commit if isolate.

oncall-bot: Runbook: high tail latency -> 1) add label canary=true to pod set 2) divert new traffic via routing policy 3) rollback canary if >=15% p99 breach persists for 10m. https://runbook.redwood.example/latency-spike
Pranav (infra): let's bisect quickly: can we toggle kernel_selection back to default on canary without full rollback? if yes, we can test which change caused regression.
Jess (runtime): yes. patch ready. I'm going to apply kernel_selection=default on 2 canary shards now and watch. command:
```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime-canary KERNEL_SELECTION=default --record
```
(5m later)
Jess (runtime): updated 2/4 canary shards. p99 on those shards dropped from ~1.2s -> ~480ms. p99 on the other 2 still ~1.3s. :white_check_mark:
Pranav (infra): strong signal kernel selector is culprit. can we roll that change out as a revert in canary, and then do a controlled recompile for the kernel?
Eva (ml-infra): agree. the JIT-1.7 compiled kernel has slight numeric/path differences that select different matmul kernels for long seqlen. we'll rebuild with alternative tiling flags.
Lisa (perf): also think batching window uptick amplifies the effect — but kernel is primary. We should revert kernel selection now and do a separate canary for batching later.
Jess (runtime): rolling back kernel selector change for all canaries. running:
```
helm upgrade runtime --set kernel_selection=default --namespace runtime --reuse-values
```
monitoring-bot: NOTE: rollout started for runtime canary revert at 2026-03-12T10:34:12Z

(10m later)
monitoring-bot: p95/p99 on canary nodes returning to baseline. p99 fell to ~580ms cluster-wide. Alerts auto-resolved. :tada:
Kate (sre): good. follow-ups: create a small perf test that runs long-seq synthetic traces through the JIT-1.7 kernels in CI, add a canary gating check comparing p99 by seq_len buckets.
Pranav (infra): also add a temporary routing rule to avoid sending >512 seq requests to canary until kernel is validated. simple fix: router config: `max_seq_canary: 512`
Sahil (runtime): I'll open PR to split kernel selection and batching changes into separate rollouts and add an automated bisect script we can run next time to flip individual flags.
Jess (runtime): summarizing actions taken: 1) identified p99 spike correlated to long-seq traffic on canary 2) bisected to kernel_selection change (jit compiled kernels) 3) reverted kernel_selection on canary 4) monitoring shows latency recovery 5) next: rebuild kernels with alternate flags, add CI perf tests, separate batching rollout, update routing policy.
Kate (sre): can someone add a short incident note in incidents/ and assign follow-ups? I'll own the postmortem if we need it.
Jess (runtime): created incident stub: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-042. added follow-ups and assigned to @Sahil and @Eva.
Pranav (infra): nice work. lesson: avoid multi-change canaries unless each change has per-seq_len perf validation. :thumbsup:
Jess (runtime): closing thread for now. will update if anything regresses. :wave:
